comparator.name: Bachelor Nanobiology
comparator.institution: Delft University of Technology and Erasmus University Rotterdam
comparator.sourceNotes: Current 2026–2027 Nanobiology TER Articles 3–5 and 8 control course requirements; the September 2026 chart corroborates their 180 EC. Freshly checked 8 October 2026. English instruction replaces normalized NLD-only metadata, preserving raw NLD provenance and TU Delft/Erasmus University Rotterdam institutional participation. Year one comprises twelve positions totaling 60 EC, with the first formal permissible mixed practical pair NB1430 Molecular Biology Techniques A and NB1445 Biophysics Techniques B, 4 EC each. This is a representative programme assignment, not a free student choice or a prediction of an individual assignment. The alternative is NB1435 plus NB1440; the programme informs students before 1 February 2027 and changes require permission. Year two comprises fourteen required units totaling 60 EC. Current NB2430 Nanotechnology is 3 EC; Article 11.7 prints 4 EC for an older-cohort transition and does not override the current entrant table. Year three is an approved 30-EC minor, NB3000 Bachelor End Project 20 EC and four distinct 2.5-EC electives totaling 10 EC. The electives are the first four formal list entries: NB3015 A Primer in Neuroscience, NB3024 Advanced Math Topics, NB3026 Biomolecular Ultrasound and NB3014 Computational Neuroscience. Selection follows formal order independently of UCR fit; catalogue prerequisites, capacity, enrolment and actual octal availability remain conditions, so this is not an exact future timetable. Outside electives and self-composed minors require Board approval. BEP admission requires all 60 first-year EC plus at least 60 EC from years two and three combined; an approved programme supervisor is required. No alternative pair, minor content or embedded skills adds credits.
